description: Compare a binding-power PrattParser against a tiered RDParser and verify that both build identical ASTs on arithmetic expressions.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Tokenize numbers, operators, and parentheses with tokenize(src), and define the left-binding-power table LBP = {'+': 10, '-': 10, '*': 20, '/': 20}.
In PrattParser, nud(tok) handles prefix tokens (numbers, parentheses, unary minus with rbp 100), while led(tok, left) parses the right operand of an infix operator by calling self.expression(bp).
In expression(self, rbp=0), parse a prefix nud(tok) and keep folding infix operators via led as long as the next operator's op_bp exceeds rbp.

steps.answer: After '+' calls self.expression(10), '*' has op_bp 20 > 10 so the inner while loop consumes '* 4'. Then '-' has op_bp 10 <= 10, which breaks the inner loop. It returns ('*', 3, 4) as the right child of '+'.
steps.question: When parsing '2+3*4-1', why does '+' pull in '3*4' as its right child but stop before '-'?

steps.description: Implement the four-tier RDParser (parse_addsub, parse_muldiv, parse_unary, parse_primary) and compare pratt_parse(t) with rd_parse(t) across four test expressions.
Start stepping through PrattParser('2+3*4-1').expression(0) as it consumes the first token.

title: Pratt Parsing vs. Tiered Recursive Descent
